name: Rhode Island
agency: Rhode Island Department of Environmental Management, Division of Law Enforcement

rule.hpNote: propulsion machinery of more than 10 hp; any PWC operator regardless of age
rule.textEn: Anyone born on or after Jan. 1, 1986 needs a boating safety certificate to run a vessel with more than 10 hp, and every PWC operator needs one whatever their age.
rule.textEs: Quien nació el 1 de enero de 1986 o después necesita un certificado de seguridad náutica para manejar una embarcación de más de 10 hp, y todo operador de moto acuática lo necesita sin importar su edad.

exemptions: Operator in training directly supervised by someone 18+ on board who meets the requirement.
Holders of a valid commercial vessel operator license (USCG, a state or a province).
Non-residents visiting who meet their home-state rules.
nonResident: Visitors who meet their home-state rules are exempt; any NASBLA-approved course certificate is accepted.
rental: Liveries renting boats over 10 hp must have renters without a certificate watch a short safety video and pass a written test.
penalty: First offense: take an approved course; second offense: fine up to $100.

sources.publisher: Rhode Island General Assembly, R.I. Gen. Laws §46-22-9.8 (Wayback Machine copy of 2025-03-28)
sources.quote: No person born on or after January 1, 1986 shall operate a vessel that is fitted with propulsion machinery of more than ten (10) horsepower on the waters of this state unless the person shall have successfully completed a boating safety education program
